title: Dividing fractions: the method and the why
sub: You already know keep, flip, change. This week: why it works, mixed numbers, and checking your answer. About 20 minutes on screen, then the written paper.
target: AQA gives method marks for working you write down. Write each step, and check every division by multiplying back.

sections.sub: Last week: multiplying fractions. From memory.

blocks.why: The reciprocal is the fraction flipped: [[5/6]] becomes [[6/5]]. Check: [[5/6]] × [[6/5]] = 1. A number times its reciprocal always makes 1. The “flip” in keep, flip, change is the reciprocal.

sections.h: 2. Core skill: why keep, flip, change works
sections.sub: Know the reason, and you can never get the method backwards.

blocks.html: Division asks “how many fit?” 6 ÷ 2 asks how many 2s fit into 6 (three). So 6 ÷ [[1/2]] asks how many halves fit into 6. Each whole has 2 halves, so 6 wholes have 12 halves. 6 ÷ [[1/2]] = 12 = 6 × 2. Dividing by [[1/2]] is the same as multiplying by 2, its reciprocal.

blocks.why: How many thirds fit into 4? Each whole has 3 thirds, so 4 wholes have 12. 4 ÷ [[1/3]] = 4 × 3 = 12.

blocks.q: Without working it out: is 5 ÷ [[2/3]] bigger or smaller than 5?
blocks.why: Dividing by a number less than 1 gives a bigger answer, because more than one of the pieces fits into each whole. Use this as a check: if you divide by a fraction less than 1 and your answer got smaller, something went wrong.

traps.msg: You multiplied without flipping. Keep [[3/5]], flip [[3/10]] to [[10/3]], then multiply.
You flipped the first fraction instead of the second. Keep the first, flip the second.

blocks.q: A jug holds [[2 1/4]] litres of juice. Each glass holds [[3/8]] of a litre. How many glasses can be filled?

traps.msg: You multiplied. “How many glasses fit?” is a division: [[2 1/4]] ÷ [[3/8]].

blocks.h: Give it as a mixed number
blocks.q: Work out [[5/6]] ÷ [[2/9]]. Give your answer as a mixed number.
blocks.formMsg: [[15/4]] is the right value, but the question asks for a mixed number. That loses the last mark.

blocks.q: Explain why 6 ÷ [[1/2]] gives the same answer as 6 × 2. Use the words how many in your answer.
starters: Dividing by a half asks how many…

points.t: says that ÷ [[1/2]] asks how many halves fit into 6
says there are 2 halves in each whole, so 6 wholes have 6 × 2 = 12 halves

mark.note: This is the “why” behind keep, flip, change. If you can explain it, you will never flip the wrong fraction.

blocks.html: Print the written paper and do it by hand. Write every step, and under each answer write a check: multiply your answer by the number you divided by. Answers on the last page.

items: I changed mixed numbers to improper fractions before flipping.
I kept the first fraction and flipped the second.
I simplified my answer and gave it in the form asked.
I checked a division by multiplying back.
I can explain why ÷ [[1/2]] is the same as × 2.

blocks.note: For the parent: listen for “how many halves fit into 6: there are 2 in each whole, so 12”. “Because of keep, flip, change” is the rule, not the reason: ask “but why does flipping work?”
